items.bold: TRUMP CANCELLED Witkoff+Kushner trip — "Too much work." Talks shifting to telephone.
items.text: NPR, CNN, Times of Israel confirmed: After Araghchi left Islamabad on Saturday, Trump posted on Truth Social: "I just cancelled the trip of my representatives going to Islamabad, Pakistan, to meet with the Iranians. Too much time wasted on traveling, too much work!" He added: "Besides which, there is tremendous infighting and confusion within their 'leadership.' Nobody knows who is in charge, including them. Also, we have all the cards, they have none!" Trump told reporters at Air Force One: "We're not going to spend 15 hours in airplanes all the time going back and forth to be giving a document that was not good enough, and so we'll deal by telephone, and they can call us anytime they want." Critically — Trump told Axios reporter Barak Ravid: cancellation does NOT mean resumption of war. "No. It doesn't mean that. We haven't thought about it yet."

items.bold: ARAGHCHI delivered "comprehensive" response to Pakistan — RETURNING TO ISLAMABAD SUNDAY before Moscow.
items.text: Iran International confirmed Araghchi delivered a "comprehensive" response during Pakistan meetings. PBS confirmed: "In Pakistan, Araghchi met with Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif about what he called Iran's red lines for negotiations." IRNA then reported: Araghchi is expected to return to Islamabad on Sunday before travelling to Russia. Part of the Iranian delegation returned to Tehran after the Islamabad talks for "consultations and to receive further instructions on issues related to the war." This return for instructions suggests Iran is actively preparing its next position — not abandoning talks. The comprehensive response delivered to Pakistan + the Islamabad return Sunday + Moscow visit signals a multi-step diplomatic process, not a collapse.

items.bold: Iran parliament deputy speaker Nikzad (state TV): "No meetings with Americans in Pakistan or Oman."
items.text: Iran International confirmed: Iran's parliament deputy speaker Ali Nikzad told state television: "Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will have no meetings with Americans in Pakistan or Oman. The public should know that Araghchi is holding no talks with the Americans on the nuclear issue." This is Iran's hardline public position — maintained consistently. The paradox: Araghchi delivered Iran's comprehensive negotiating demands to Pakistan (Reuters), is returning to Islamabad Sunday (IRNA), and then heading to Moscow as guarantor country. Iran is actively engaged diplomatically while publicly denying it. Iran International's headline — "Araghchi passes on comprehensive response in Pakistan talks" — and Nikzad's denial are not contradictory: Iran is talking to Pakistan (the mediator), not to Americans directly.

items.bold: USS Pinckney intercepted vessel via helicopter — 37 ships redirected total. Air defense in Kermanshah.
items.text: Iran International and CNN confirmed: M/V Sevan intercepted by a US Navy helicopter operating from guided-missile destroyer USS Pinckney in the Arabian Sea — just one day after being added to US sanctions lists. The vessel is now "complying with orders to turn back toward Iran under US military escort." This brings total vessels redirected to 37 since blockade began April 13. CENTCOM: blockade enforcement continues. Separately: Iran International cited Mehr News Agency — multiple air defense sounds heard in western Iranian city of Kermanshah and surrounding areas. Cause unconfirmed as of 8 AM IST. No confirmed new US or Israeli strike. Possible defensive test or false alarm. Requires monitoring.

items.bold: PM Sharif "warm and constructive" call with Pezeshkian. Iran Air resumed international flights.
items.text: Iran International confirmed: Pakistan PM Sharif had a "warm and constructive" phone call with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian Saturday evening about the evolving regional situation. Sharif "appreciated Iran's continued engagement, including the high-level delegation to Islamabad led by FM Araghchi." Pakistan reaffirmed commitment to acting as "an honest and sincere facilitator" toward durable peace. Separately (PBS confirmed): Iran Air resumed international flights Saturday for the first time since the war began February 28. Routes launched: Tehran to Istanbul, Muscat, and Medina (Saudi Arabia). This is a significant normalisation signal — Iran suspended all international flights February 28 expecting US airstrikes on airports. Resuming them signals Iran calculates the ceasefire is structurally stable enough for civilian aviation.

items.bold: Spain threatened with NATO suspension over Iran war base refusal. Senator Graham praised cancellation.
items.text: NPR confirmed: Reuters reported a confidential US communication suggesting Spain could be suspended from NATO and blocked from top alliance positions — this after Spain refused to allow the US to use bases on Spanish territory for the Iran war and declared the war "illegal." Spanish PM Sanchez: "We don't work on the basis of emails. We are working on official documents and positions." This is the most serious NATO internal rift of the war. Separately: Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC) praised Trump's cancellation of the Witkoff-Kushner trip, saying Tehran had responded to the ceasefire extension with more attacks on international shipping — making the case for the hawkish position that talks are futile and pressure should continue.

assessment.body:
Sunday 8 AM IST. The diplomacy shifted gears overnight — from Islamabad to phone lines and Oman.

WHAT HAPPENED SATURDAY — THE FULL CONFIRMED SEQUENCE
• Araghchi arrived Islamabad Friday evening (AFP photo confirmed)
• Saturday: Araghchi met PM Sharif + Field Marshal Munir — discussed Iran's red lines (PBS)
• Araghchi delivered "comprehensive" response to Pakistan (Iran International)
• Araghchi left Islamabad Saturday → flew to Muscat, Oman (IRNA/PBS/AP)
• Trump posted on Truth Social: cancelled Witkoff+Kushner trip — "Too much work, call us"
• Trump at Air Force One: "Not going to spend 15 hours in airplanes for a document not good enough"
• Critical clarification — Trump to Axios: cancellation NOT resumption of war
• IRNA: Araghchi RETURNING to Islamabad Sunday before Moscow
• Part of Iranian delegation returned to Tehran for consultations and further instructions

WHY THIS IS NOT A COLLAPSE
• Iran delivered a "comprehensive" response — not a blank rejection
• Araghchi is coming back to Islamabad Sunday — proximity talks continuing
• PM Sharif had "warm and constructive" call with Pezeshkian Saturday evening
• Oman stop (historic Iran-US back-channel) + Moscow (Russia as guarantor) + Sunday Islamabad return = deal architecture active
• Trump explicitly said cancellation ≠ war resumption
• Iran Air resumed international flights (Istanbul, Muscat, Medina) — Iran expects ceasefire to hold

THE HARDLINE SIGNALS (BOTH SIDES)
• Iran parliament deputy speaker Nikzad (state TV): "No meetings with Americans. No nuclear talks."
• Trump: "Nobody knows who is in charge in Iran, including them. We have all the cards."
• Senator Graham praised the cancellation — hawkish pressure on Trump from Senate
• Iran IRGC warning: strong response if blockade continues
• USS Pinckney intercepted 37th ship — blockade tightening

THE Kermanshah UNKNOWN
• Air defense sounds heard in western Iranian city of Kermanshah
• No confirmed new US or Israeli strike as of 8 AM IST
• Requires monitoring before India market open Monday 9:15 AM

INDIA'S MONDAY OPEN
• Nifty closed Friday at 23,897 — below 24,000
• Three-day -2,592 Sensex fall last week
• Araghchi Islamabad return Sunday + Oman back-channel + Moscow = talks not dead
• Trump cancellation + 37 ship blockade + air defense sounds = risks remain
• 35% talks signal → Nifty 24,000-24,300
• 40% phone stalemate → Nifty 23,700-24,000
• 25% incident → Nifty below 23,500

VERDICT: Saturday's sequence is best described as a choreographed diplomatic dance — both sides maintaining their public positions (Iran: we're not talking to Americans; Trump: too much work, call us) while the actual negotiating machinery continues through Pakistan and now Oman. Araghchi delivered Iran's comprehensive demands. He's returning to Islamabad Sunday. He's heading to Moscow for Russian guarantees. The ceasefire holds. Iran Air is flying again internationally. This is the West Asia War's diplomatic framework functioning at its most sophisticated level — just not the way anyone expected or announced it would.
